PullRequest.Title: Refactor hiddenModelN prompts to reduce complexity
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- Add guidance to hiddenModelN to avoid excessive changes, unnecessary files and complexity, and unrelated cleanup.
- Encourage reading relevant repository instructions and nearby code, tests, documentation, and CI, with clean, mergeable code as the goal.
- Explicitly discourage excessive test files while preserving the original guidance on repository conventions and reuse of utilities, tests, and helpers verbatim.
- Keep the change confined to the existing engineering-judgment section; no new files.

## Validation
- Targeted Copilot ESLint passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Pre-commit hygiene completed; root hygiene excludes Copilot files, which have their own lint rules.
- Copilot compile was attempted but is blocked by the local esbuild executable failing with `spawn EFTYPE` (invalid application for this OS platform). Rebuilding esbuild did not resolve the environment issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: A coding request handled by hiddenModelN through the agent tool-calling loop
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each serial tool-loop iteration resolves the model prompt, renders AgentPrompt (including HiddenModelNPrompt), serializes the messages, and sends them through endpoint.makeChatRequest2 before the iteration can receive a response. The diff adds three static bullets to that system prompt. Background compaction can be off the immediate critical path, but its unchanged request may reuse the rendered main-message prefix.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send rendered chat messages and tool schemas to the model endpoint via makeChatRequest2
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pre-existing model request per awaited runOne iteration; iterations are serial and can continue to the configured tool-call limit (with an autopilot cap of 200). The diff adds a fixed three-bullet payload to each applicable request but adds no requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request was sent once per iteration with the same surrounding hiddenModelN system prompt, minus the three added bullets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request is on the critical path for every agent-loop response. The added bytes/tokens are bounded and do not change request count or scheduling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Model-selected reads/searches of relevant repository instructions, nearby code, tests, documentation, or CI configuration using existing agent tools
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Not statically determined: the new guidance is conditional on relevance and does not invoke a tool itself, name a mandatory tool, enumerate files, or establish per-file fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prompt already instructed the model to follow repository conventions, reuse existing utilities/tests/helpers, and keep edits scoped, but did not explicitly mention inspecting nearby documentation and CI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Any model-chosen inspection tool would occupy later serial agent iterations, but the diff does not prove that an additional boundary call occurs for a realistic request or set its cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The deterministic payload cost is O(I), where I is the number of model invocations in the serial tool loop, with a fixed three-bullet delta per invocation; it does not scale with repository size or file count. Potential inspection work is model-selected and has no diff-defined multiplicity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The main loop awaits runOne before starting the next iteration, so applicable model requests are serial. Existing background summarization may overlap, but the diff does not change its trigger, concurrency, or request cardinality.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AgentPrompt is rendered on each request. The added text is in a stable system-prefix position and is eligible for any existing provider/prompt-prefix caching; no cache key, breakpoint, invalidation, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior changes. Cold and warm requests both carry the same bounded logical prompt delta, while provider-side processing savings are endpoint-dependent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the fixed text is rendered and sent once per applicable model invocation; low confidence that it causes any extra repository-inspection call because that depends on model behavior and task relevance.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact tokenizer count, wire encoding, provider prefix-cache hit rate, and whether the model changes its tool choices are not established. The deterministic increase is only three fixed bullets; no evidence ties it to measurable latency, throughput loss, or context-compaction churn.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR creates only a small bounded serialization/token increase on an existing network request, with no new boundary call, fan-out, concurrency burst, retention, or credible user-visible performance impact. The behavioral instruction is insufficient evidence of deterministic extra tool work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed hunk and traced hiddenModelN prompt selection, per-iteration prompt rendering, the serial tool-calling loop, model network submission, provider-cache considerations, and possible model-directed repository inspection. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
